items.name: FX_DELAY_TIME_RANGE
items.doc: The FX delay's time travel. `max` is the NATIVE ring's ceiling — the same number as `OMX_FXDELAY_MAX_MS` in `omx_delay.h`, pinned to it by the engine's conformance test. Distinct from the per-route ALIGNMENT delay (`OUTPUT_DELAY_RANGE`, 1 s, `OMX_DELAY_MAX_MS`): one is a musical echo with feedback and mix, the other is a pure latency. Two facts, two rings, two ceilings — sharing the word "delay" is why they keep being confused for each other.

items.name: FX_DELAY_FEEDBACK_RANGE
items.doc: The FX delay's REGENERATION travel — how much of the wet tail feeds back in. Stops short of 1: unity feedback is a runaway the kernel hard-clamps anyway, so offering it would draw travel the DSP refuses. Not NORMALIZED_RANGE for exactly that reason — it is a 0..1 quantity whose top the DSP does not accept, and a control must not offer a value its actuator will eat.

items.name: DELAY_TONE_RANGE
items.doc: The FX delay's TONE — a NORMALIZED_RANGE instance with its own come-up value, matching the console's delay default tone. See REVERB_SIZE_RANGE for why this is a named constant rather than a default on the shared shape.

items.name: DELAY_MIX_RANGE
items.doc: The FX DELAY's wet/dry — the same split as REVERB_MIX_RANGE, its own declaration.

items.name: FX_DELAY_PINGPONG_DEFAULT
items.doc: The FX delay's PING-PONG come-up value — a toggle, so it has no travel, only this. Declared here rather than as a literal in the console's delay default state (which now reads it) so the DPF plugin generator (omx-plugins) reads the same fact the desk seeds a fresh strip with.

items.name: DELAY_PINGPONGS

source.origin: omx-dsp a624f26 include/omxdsp/fx/omx_delay.h:45 struct omx_fx_delay.pingpong, read at :190; the console engine's delay state seeds ping-pong from the same default; omx-plugins 7461cdd plugins/omx-delay/omx_delay_instance.h:155

items.doc: The FX delay's PING-PONG switch: on cross-feeds the two legs' feedback, so each leg's repeats come from the other leg's damped tap and the echoes bounce L<->R (`omx_delay.h`'s `struct omx_fx_delay.pingpong`, read where the feedback is formed). A live control on the console's delay row (`DelayState.pingpong`) and on the omx-delay plugin. Its come-up value is FX_DELAY_PINGPONG_DEFAULT, by reference, so the default keeps one home.

items.name: FX_DELAY_TAPS_RANGE

source.origin: omx-dsp 88471a8 include/omxdsp/fx/omx_delay.h:41 OMX_FXDELAY_MAX_TAPS 4, :53 struct omx_fx_delay.ntaps 1..OMX_FXDELAY_MAX_TAPS (0 is the one-tap delay); the console engine's delay row takes the same 1..4

items.doc: How many integer read taps of the FX delay's one ring are engaged. 1 is the one-tap delay, bit for bit; `max` is the tap-array ceiling the kernel sizes its arrays by, so the arrays and the travel are one fact. An array extent is an integer constant: the C reader takes OMX_FX_DELAY_TAPS_RANGE_MAX (4) for `OMX_FXDELAY_MAX_TAPS` in `omx_delay.h`, never the alias OMX_DELAY_TAPS_MAX, which is the float 4.0f.

items.name: DELAY_TAP_LIMITS

source.origin: omx-dsp 88471a8 include/omxdsp/fx/omx_delay.h omx_fxdelay_tap_gains: per-tap gain 0..1 and balance-law pan -1..+1; the come-up values are the console engine's delay tap defaults (tap 0 unity at centre, taps 1..3 a triple pattern)

items.doc: The legal range of each read tap's gain (0..1) and pan (-1..+1, the balance law's travel), keyed by the delay row's own field, with each tap's come-up value. Tap 0 comes up at unity gain, centre: the one-tap delay. Taps 1..3 come up as a usable triple pattern (an eighth left, a dotted eighth right, a dotted quarter centre), so raising the tap count is musical at once.

items.name: DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_NUMS

source.origin: omx-dsp 0f23bed test/fx/delay_taps.test.c:59-60 TAP_NUM {1,1,3,1,2,3,1,4,3,2,3} and TAP_DEN {4,3,8,2,3,4,1,3,2,1,1}, the tap oracle's factor set in its declared order; the console engine's delay taps carry the same eleven members in the same order (1/4 .. 3)

items.doc: The numerators of the FX delay's tap factor set, in member order: 1/4, 1/3, 3/8, 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, 1, 4/3, 3/2, 2, 3. A read tap k >= 1 sits at the base time times numerator / denominator (DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_DENS at the same position), rounded once to samples. The set is two integer lists, not a set of ids, because a factor such as 1/2 is no id the schema accepts and the ratio must stay exact (1/3 has no finite decimal).

items.name: DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_DENS

source.origin: omx-dsp 0f23bed test/fx/delay_taps.test.c:59-60 TAP_NUM {1,1,3,1,2,3,1,4,3,2,3} and TAP_DEN {4,3,8,2,3,4,1,3,2,1,1}, the tap oracle's factor set in its declared order; the console engine's delay taps carry the same eleven members in the same order (1/4 .. 3)

items.doc: The denominators of the FX delay's tap factor set, in member order, one per numerator of DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_NUMS: the factor at position i is DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_NUMS[i] / DELAY_TAP_FACTOR_DENS[i].
